subject: Private deployment: network boundary & PII/data controls — post-call items
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Christina Park <christina@quietbasin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network boundary & PII/data controls — post-call items

Thanks again for taking time this morning, Christina — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and suggested next steps so we can get your security and networking teams unblocked.\n\nHighlights from the call:
- Quiet Basin requirement: no customer PII may be persisted outside Quiet Basin-controlled storage.
- Deployment preference: Private (VPC) with optional on-prem/air-gapped mode for regulated workloads.
- Network: strict egress policy, explicit NAT egress IP ranges, and no outbound access to third-party telemetry unless approved.
- Logging: need redactable request logs and a 90-day retention default with the option for shorter windows per endpoint.

Action items we committed to: 
1) Send a short security summary + SOC2 artifacts for initial review (attached).
2) Draft a proposed network boundary diagram showing where Redwood components would reside and egress points.
3) Clarify logging controls: what we record by default, how encryption-at-rest + KMS works, and how to enable PII redaction at ingestion.
4) Identify on-prem constraints for the air-gapped scenario (physical media for model weights, local PKI, and offline orchestration).

Next meetings:
- Technical deep-dive with Quiet Basin network/security team (proposed Wed 24 Mar, 10am PT).
- Internal alignment with our infra/security (Grace + Tessa) before the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood-security-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope, encryption, KMS integrations), quietbasin-network-draft.png (placeholder network sketch).

If that looks right, I will: upload a more detailed architecture diagram with NAT/egress flow, and a short doc listing exact logging fields we retain and which are redactable.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0133
From: Christina Park <christina@quietbasin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@quietbasin.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network boundary & PII/data controls — post-call items

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We cannot allow raw customer emails or SSNs to be logged in any persistent store outside of Quiet Basin. Session caching for performance is OK if the cache is ephemeral and never written to disk.
- Retention: default 30 days for request metadata, 90 days for anonymized aggregated metrics; PII must be deletable on-demand.
- Egress: we require a single static egress IP (or tight range) per deployment and DNS allow-listing. No third-party outbound calls without explicit whitelisting; telemetry to Redwood's hosted analytics is currently a blocker.
- On-prem scenario: our Security Ops will want a checklist for air-gapped install steps and a list of required ports/services (we run hardened RHEL).

Please provide the network diagram and a table of log fields with redaction toggles before the deep-dive so our PM/security can pre-review. Also, include the expected operator privileges (what our sysadmins will need to run the stack).

— Christina
Director of Platform Security, Quiet Basin Industries
christina@quietbasin.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Christina Park <christina@quietbasin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network boundary & PII/data controls — post-call items

Christina — great questions. Quick answers inline and attachments + links below.\n\n- PII persistence: Redwood Private does not persist raw prompts or responses to long-term storage unless explicitly enabled. KV/prefix caches are kept in-memory by default; on-disk persistence is opt-in and requires explicit customer config. We can provide a written attestation and sample config snippet to disable disk-backed cache.\n\n- Retention: we can set request-metadata retention to 30 days as a deployment default. Aggregated metrics for ops can be reduced to a 90-day window and anonymized before export. For deletions, we support an on-demand purge endpoint that removes data from our control plane indexing within SLA (we'll include SLA targets in the tech doc).\n\n- Egress: we will publish the exact egress CIDR ranges for the private deployment. For Quiet Basin's air-gapped requirement, we support a model where all outbound access is disabled and packages are installed via signed artifacts you provide (offline repo). For VPC deployments we can also pin a single Elastic IP per cluster.\n\n- Logging controls: attached is a table of candidate log fields with flags for retain/redact/never-record. We also support tokenization hooks for customer-side PII tokenization before sending.\n\nNext steps (we propose):
1) I will upload a refined network diagram showing: customer subnet -> private Redwood control plane (customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink) -> NAT/egress (single IP) -> optional on-prem sync. (ETA Tue EOD)
2) Grace/Tessa will prepare an operator-privileges checklist and an air-gap install playbook draft.
3) Schedule the deep-dive with Quiet Basin security on Wed 24 Mar 10am PT — confirm if that still works.

Attachments: redwood-security-summary.pdf, quietbasin-network-draft.png
Links: HubSpot deal RDW-3471 (internal), architecture draft (Drive).

Thanks — will follow up with the artifacts.
Jonas
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment: network boundary & PII/data controls — post-call items

Jonas / Tessa — quick internal checklist before we send the refined diagram to Quiet Basin:
- [ ] Produce an architecture PNG that explicitly labels: control plane VPC (customer-managed), inference worker subnets, KV cache behavior (mem-only vs disk), NAT/Egress IPs placeholder, and optional on-prem sync boundary.
- [ ] Create a log-field table (CSV) with columns: field_name, default_retention_days, redactability (yes/no), storage_location (ephemeral | control-plane-index | customer-specified).
- [ ] Draft air-gap install doc with: signed artifact hashing, offline dependency bundle, local KMS integration notes, and supported OS versions (RHEL 8+).
- [ ] Identify a single staffer who will be the Quiet Basin technical contact (Jonas: ask Christina).
- [ ] Confirm our target SLA for purge requests (we'll propose 48 hours for control-plane indexing purge).

I will take the arch PNG and the purge SLA text. Tessa, can you draft the log-field CSV and the air-gap outline? Jonas, please confirm the Wed 24 slot and Christina's technical contact.

Grace
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
